diagnosis.what_happened: A regular expression replacement intended to remove footnotes obliterated the entire body text of a docx document.
diagnosis.behavior_caused_outcome: Using unanchored regex on minified OpenXML (word/document.xml) which lacked newline boundaries caused non-greedy wildcards to match from the first paragraph tag to the end of the document.
diagnosis.what_should_have_happened: Structured XML DOM parsing via lxml or ElementTree should have been used. A mechanical pre-flight paragraph count verification should have been executed before release.
diagnosis.rationale_why: OpenXML documents are typically minified, single-line serializations where standard text-processing heuristics like line boundaries fail catastrophically.

desired_behavior: Strictly ban regex string substitutions on minified XML. Mandate structured XML DOM parsing via lxml or ElementTree for all OpenXML modifications. Mandate mechanical body paragraph count verification (> 0) before release.
generalization: Never use regex for structural modification of minified XML files like OpenXML.

evidence.observed_value: Entire body paragraph narrative was deleted
evidence.threshold_value: Zero tolerance for body text obliteration
